claims.text: Uber Eats customers in Spring, a suburb north of Houston, became the first in the country to order food delivered by a Zipline drone through Uber Eats, on Tuesday, November 17th.
claims.quote: Uber Eats customers in Spring, Texas, a suburb north of Houston, became the first in the country on Tuesday, November 17,

claims.text: The drone does not land. It hovers over the yard and lowers the order on a tether.
claims.quote: It hovers over the yard, lowers dinner on a tether, and leaves.

claims.text: The drones carry orders of up to eight pounds.
claims.quote: carrying orders of up to eight pounds as far as 10 miles from the restaurant

claims.text: Orders fly as far as 10 miles from the restaurant.
claims.quote: carrying orders of up to eight pounds as far as 10 miles from the restaurant

claims.text: The drones cruise at about 300 feet at speeds of up to 70 miles per hour.

claims.quote: CTE drone team students placed and received the first order.

claims.quote: Spring is unincorporated Harris County.

cautions: Say first for Uber Eats by Zipline drone, never the first drone food delivery. Zipline has delivered food in DFW for a long time.
Spring as the launch suburb comes from journalism. Zipline's own post says Houston.
Voice the Spring service hours, 8 a.m. to 10 p.m., not the aircraft's 24/7.
Altitude differs by source. Do not merge about 300, more than 300 and roughly 330 feet into one exact figure.
Under 10 minutes is an Uber executive's quote, not a measured average.
People still cook and pack the order. Remote pilots monitor and can override (Zipline's general model, a 2024 post). Do not say no human is involved.
The FAA environmental assessment for Zipline's Texas metros was still a draft on November 18th per DroneXL. Do not claim full regulatory sign-off.
Only eligible addresses can order. Do not say all of Spring can order by drone.
Do not give an exact Round Rock launch date.
Use pod on a tether, not a product name.
